title: The Go SDK's response cache and request deduplication

prose.text: The SDK can cache GET responses and collapse identical GETs into one request. Providers that turn this on inherit its behavior on every read. {{zia-provider-enables-cache}} {{expired-entry-survives-cleanup}}

checks.do: Whether a stale result after a write from the same client, within the cache lifetime, is a cached read rather than a server fault.

zia-provider-enables-cache.statement: The ZIA Terraform provider sets `zscaler.WithCache(true)`, a 10-minute cache lifetime and an 8-minute value it labels the idle timeout on the SDK configuration it builds for its OneAPI client. In the SDK, the first of those two durations is the entry lifetime and the second is the cleanup interval passed to `NewCache`.

quotes: zscaler.WithCacheTtl(10 * time.Minute), // Cache entries for 10 minutes
zscaler.WithCacheTti(8 * time.Minute),  // Idle timeout of 8 minutes
// Initialize the client with the configuration v3Client, err := zscaler.NewOneAPIClient(config)
func NewCache(ttl, cleanWindow time.Duration, maxCacheSizeMB int) (Cache, error) {

waiters-ignore-cancellation.statement: With the cache enabled, when a non-sandbox GET for the same URL is already in flight, later GETs for that URL wait for it on a plain wait group, so a cancelled or timed-out caller stays blocked until the first request finishes.

quotes: // Check if there's an in-flight request for the same URL
existingIfr.wg.Wait() // Wait for the in-flight request to complete

owner-error-not-shared.statement: If the first in-flight GET fails, waiting callers do not receive its error: the error and response fields they check are never set, so each waiter sends the request again.
owner-error-not-shared.conditions: The reads are quoted. That nothing assigns the in-flight record's err, resp, or result was established by searching the file at v3.8.44 and HEAD; absence cannot be quoted.

quotes: // If no error but not cached, something went wrong - proceed with normal request

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK cache contract) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

two-owners-possible.statement: Claiming a URL as in flight is a separate check and store rather than one atomic step, so two GETs that miss the cache at the same moment can both send the request.
two-owners-possible.conditions: Absence claim (check and store not atomic): `grep -c LoadOrStore zscaler/oneapiconfig.go` returns 0 at v3.8.44 and at v3.8.58, and `grep -n 'Lock()' zscaler/oneapiconfig.go` at v3.8.58 finds locks only in startTokenRenewalTicker, Close, authenticate and the token refresh inside ExecuteRequest (`c.Lock() // Prevent concurrent token refresh`), none around the cache-miss Load and Store (the same four functions at v3.8.44).

write-invalidates-but-inflight-get-repop.statement: Up to v3.8.57, a write clears the cached entries for its URL and parent collection before it is sent, and caching a GET response is unconditional, so a GET that started before the write took effect can store the pre-write response after the invalidation, and that response is then served until it expires. From v3.8.58 the SDK registers each write and each GET, and a GET that overlaps a write affecting its key is not cached, unless the write starts between the overlap check and the store (gap cache-done-then-set-window).
write-invalidates-but-inflight-get-repop.conditions: Up to v3.8.57 this needs a GET to start before a write and finish after it; the code allows it, and how often it happens depends on timing. From v3.8.58 the overlap check covers a write in flight when the GET starts or that starts or finishes while it is in flight; the source does not say whether a write that starts between the overlap check and the store is covered (gap cache-done-then-set-window).

quotes: // Register the write before invalidating: a GET of an invalidated key
// that is in flight now, or that starts before the write finishes, may
// return the data from before the write and must not be cached. Entries
not caching response that overlapped a write
// read whose key starts with one of the prefixes of a write that was in flight
// when the read started, or that started or finished while the read was in
// flight, is marked as overlapping, and its response must not be cached.

upstream.note: Fixed in Go SDK v3.8.58 (PR 475), apart from gap cache-done-then-set-window.

parent-collection-invalidation.statement: A write also clears the parent collection's cached list. The SDK added this because a stale collection read after a child change broke the ZIA provider's rule reordering (SUP-3988).

quotes: // Also invalidate the parent collection endpoint so that list
// responses (e.g. /sslInspectionRules) are cleared when a child
// this, a GET on the collection is served stale from cache for
// up to the TTL after a child PUT/POST/DELETE, which breaks
// any client logic that mutates and immediately re-reads
//   - its parent collection, so list responses (e.g. /sslInspectionRules) are
//     cleared when a child resource (e.g. /sslInspectionRules/123) is
//     mutated. Without this, a GET on the collection is served stale from
//     cache for up to the TTL after a child PUT/POST/DELETE, which breaks any
//     client logic that mutates and immediately re-reads (e.g.
//     terraform-provider-zia rule reordering, SUP-3988). Mirrors the legacy

prefix-invalidation-over-broad.statement: Invalidation matches cache keys by raw string prefix, and a write's parent key is its URL cut at the last `/`, so a create on a top-level collection such as `/zia/api/v1/firewallFilteringRules` clears every cached read under `/zia/api/v1`. Up to v3.8.57 the match only deletes entries; from v3.8.58 the same prefixes are also registered with the write tracker, which matches them by raw string prefix too.

quotes: for _, p := range prefixes { if strings.HasPrefix(key, p) { r.overlapping = true
// Check if there's an in-flight request for the same URL

prefix-invalidation-over-broad.conditions: Absence claim (no write tracker before v3.8.58): `git grep -n -e BeginWrite -e cacheWrites -e write_tracker <release> -- .` returns nothing at v3.8.44 or v3.8.57 (cache/ holds cache.go, go-cache.go and nop-cache.go at v3.8.44, plus cache_test.go at v3.8.57); at v3.8.58 the same search finds cache/write_tracker.go and its `func (t *WriteTracker) BeginWrite(prefixes ...string) (end func()) {`.

cached-body-read-errors-ignored.statement: When serving from cache, an error reading the cached body is ignored: the caller gets whatever was read, and no error.

quotes: respData, err := io.ReadAll(cachedResp.Body) if err == nil { cachedResp.Body = io.NopCloser(bytes.NewBuffer(respData)) } c.oauth2Credentials.Logger.Printf("[INFO] served from cache, key:%s\n", key) return respData, cachedResp, req, nil

expired-entry-survives-cleanup.statement: An entry older than the cache lifetime can still be served until the next cleanup pass, which in the ZIA provider's settings runs on the 8-minute interval.
expired-entry-survives-cleanup.conditions: Rests on the cache library's behavior (bigcache's `LifeWindow` marks entries expired and `CleanWindow` sets how often expired entries are removed; a read does not check age). That library is not a registered source and the SDK's own `Get` does not check age either, so the survival of an expired entry between cleanups is an inference from the library, not something any source here states.

cache-done-then-set-window.title: Is a write that starts between the SDK's overlap check and the cache store covered?
cache-done-then-set-window.blocks: saying the v3.8.58 overlap check fully closes the stale-after-write case
cache-done-then-set-window.detail: In v3.8.58 the overlap check (Done) unregisters the read and the cache store follows as a separate step. A code reading found no statement of whether a write that starts between the two is covered, and no test in the SDK covers that ordering. This is a code reading, not verified behaviour.
